title: Prefix-hash salt omission during model manifest rollout — retrospective
body:
Summary:

During a staged rollout of model v2.6.0->v2.6.1 (quantized, sharded) we observed an increase in token latency p95 and a 3x increase in per-request token spend for a subset of production traffic routed to the canary pool in us-west-2. Responses were correct (meaningful text) but end-to-end latency and token billing increased. The canary failed health gates on cost and latency, and the rollout was aborted.

Why this is unusual / motivation for this doc:

We often see regressions caused by weight corruption or tokenizer changes. This incident instead was introduced by a manifest metadata omission that changed how prefix caching keys were computed across older and newer runtime nodes, causing persistent cache misses and duplicate generation work. That interaction between model manifest metadata and the runtime's prefix-hash computation is not fully captured in existing runbooks, so this is both a retrospective and a short runbook draft.

Timeline (UTC):
- 2024-09-12 02:07: Canary rollout started: 5% traffic to canary pool (v2.6.1).
- 2024-09-12 02:12: Automated SLO guardrails: alerts fired — token-based spend up 2.8x on canary cohort.
- 2024-09-12 02:14: Ops oncall paged (priority P1).
- 2024-09-12 02:20: Observability: p95 token latency increased from 120ms -> 420ms for canary nodes; host CPU/GPU usage normal.
- 2024-09-12 02:25: Quick investigation: KV cache hit rate for model v2.6.1 nodes was ~6% vs baseline ~78%.
- 2024-09-12 02:30: Canary rollout aborted and traffic switched back to v2.6.0 at 02:32.
- 2024-09-12 03:10: Initial root cause hypothesis formed (manifest vs runtime hashing mismatch).
- 2024-09-12 06:00: Repro harness created; reproduction verified locally with sample prompts (cache hits dropped when manifest omitted prefix-salt field).

Impact:
- Latency: p95 token latency on canary nodes increased ~3.5x while rollout was active.
- Cost: Token spend on canary cohort increased ~2.8x from redundant generation.
- Availability: No correctness regressions or error-rate increase. No customer-facing errors but degraded latency and cost SLOs.

Detection signals & how we spotted it:
- Automated rollout guardrails that check cost-per-request and p95 latency tripped on the low-volume canary cohort.
- SRE dashboards: KV cache hit rate metric for per-model per-node.
- Cost telemetry showing token spend differential between versions.
- Canary logs showing repeated re-generation of prefixes (same request id patterns).

Root cause (short):
- A recently merged manifest generation change (PR #412) removed inclusion of the optional "prefix_hash_salt" metadata from the model manifest when the salt was empty. Older runtime nodes defaulted to a zero-salt value when missing; the new manifest omission caused the runtime hash function to compute different prefix keys between older and newer nodes because the runtime runtime-config path interpreted absence differently depending on a code path introduced in 2024-07. The net effect: identical prefixes hashed to different cache keys on canary nodes -> cache misses -> repeated autoregressive work and duplicated outputs, increasing tokens and latency.

Reproduction notes (local):
1) Start local-serving runtime with v2.6.0 manifest that includes explicit prefix_hash_salt: "\"\"" (empty string) and a kv-cache warmup.
2) Issue a set of 500 sample prompts representative of production prefix distribution; observe cache hit rate ~78%.
3) Replace manifest with v2.6.1 manifest that omits prefix_hash_salt key entirely and restart nodes.
4) Re-issue same 500 prompts; observe cache hit rate drop to ~5-8% and increased token generation per request.

Why the metadata omission happened:
- The manifest template generator treats empty string salts as "not present" and prunes them. A recent tidy PR intended to reduce manifest size pruned empty metadata fields. No unit tests asserted canonicalization semantics for prefix_hash_salt.

Mitigation taken during incident:
- Immediate rollback of canary and halt of staged rollout.
- Emergency hotfix: re-generated manifests for v2.6.1 that include an explicit prefix_hash_salt: "" entry and re-run canary in a small sandbox.
- Added runtime-side safeguard: runtime now treats missing prefix_hash_salt and explicit empty-string salt as equivalent (hotfix applied on canary infra).

Postmortem analysis / root causes (detailed):
- Primary cause: manifest generator change that pruned empty-string metadata without coordinating runtime expectations.
- Secondary cause: Lack of manifest-contract tests that exercise metadata canonicalization across codepaths (manifest generator, model onboarding, runtime parsing).
- Latent cause: Rollout guardrails detected symptom (cost/latency) correctly, but there was no pre-rollout unit test or synthetic canary test covering cross-version cache key equality.

Action items (short-term):
- (A1) Add manifest contract test that ensures prefix_hash_salt canonicalization: PR in model-manifests repo. Owner: Evan Brooks. Due: 2024-09-19.
- (A2) Add synthetic canary test in CI that starts two runtimes (old and new manifest variants) and checks KV cache key equality for a small sample corpus. Owner: SRE infra. Due: 2024-09-26.
- (A3) Revert manifest pruning behavior or make it explicit; update manifest generator to always emit prefix_hash_salt explicitly, even if empty. Owner: Model Onboarding. Due: 2024-09-18.
- (A4) Runtime: add assertion/validation at model load time to log a warning when prefix_hash_salt absent and treat absence explicitly as empty string (hotfix patch already deployed as canary). Owner: Serving runtime. Due: 2024-09-15 (hotfix), 2024-10-01 (full rollout).
- (A5) Detectability: Add observability metric: per-model prefix-hash key entropy + cross-version key comparison for canaries. Owner: Observability team. Due: 2024-10-01.

Runbook draft (for similar incidents):
- Detection
  1) If rollout guardrails for cost or token-latency trip, immediately check per-model KV cache hit rates and compare across versions.
  2) Query model manifest for both versions: check presence/absence of prefix_hash_salt, token_map_version, and any metadata that affects cache key computation.
  3) If KV cache hit rate is anomalously low only on one version, instrument live canary to print (sampled) prefix hash keys for a small subset of requests and compare hashes across runtime nodes.

- Short-term remediation
  1) Abort/rollback rollout.
  2) Optional: regenerate manifest with explicit prefix_hash_salt and redeploy to canary nodes if rollback not immediately possible.
  3) If hotfixing runtime, ensure compatibility check in model load path so nodes don't compute differing keys for the same canonical prefix.

- Long-term safeguards
  1) Add manifest-schema enforcement (CI gate) that prevents pruning of fields that can impact runtime hashing semantics.
  2) Add cross-version cache-key regression test to the release pipeline.
  3) Add a small synthetic canary job that verifies cache-hit parity before moving beyond 5% traffic.

Notes / open questions:
- Is there any other metadata field we currently prune that could affect hashing (e.g., token_map_version)? Recommend a sweep of manifest generator to enumerate fields and add a "do-not-prune" list.
- Consider versioning the prefix-hash algorithm itself and exposing a manifest field that includes a canonicalization checksum so future changes are explicit.

Appendix: Relevant logs and artifacts
- Sample log excerpt: "prefix_key computed=0x3f7a12fe manifest_salt=ABSENT node_id=canary-12 request_id=..."
- Repro harness: repo link in linked artifacts.
- PR that caused omission: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-manifests/pull/412

Owner/Follow-up:
- Document owner: Maya Chen.
- Primary technical contact: Evan Brooks.
- Follow-ups scheduled on SRE weekly retro 2024-09-18.

If you see anything missing or incorrect in this writeup (especially specifics about manifest generator behavior), ping me in #sre-ops or add inline comments.
